Gas & Eye Irritation: Causes & Remedies | ASG Eye Hospital

Exposure to smoke, pollution, chemical fumes, and gas leaks can irritate the eyes and affect daily comfort. 

Common symptoms include:

• Redness

To protect your eyes:

• Avoid smoke and chemical exposure
• Wear protective eyewear in high-risk environments

If symptoms persist, worsen, or affect your vision, seek professional eye care promptly.

LASIK vs Contact Lenses – Which is Better for Students? | ASG Eye Hospital

Students today spend long hours studying, attending classes, using digital devices, and participating in sports or extracurricular activities. Clear vision is essential, making many students choose between contact lenses and LASIK surgery.

Contact lenses offer temporary vision correction, but they require daily cleaning, proper hygiene, and ongoing maintenance. Extended wear can sometimes lead to dryness, irritation, and an increased risk of eye infections.

LASIK surgery, on the other hand, provides long-term vision correction and reduces dependence on glasses or contact lenses. For eligible students with a stable eye prescription, 

LASIK offers several advantages:

• Freedom from daily lens maintenance
• No recurring costs for lenses and solutions
• Greater convenience during sports and activities
• Improved comfort during long study sessions
• Reduced dependence on vision correction accessories

Modern LASIK eye surgery uses advanced diagnostic technology to create personalized treatment plans with high precision and safety. Most students can return to their routine within a few days.

Best Eye Specialist for Retina Problems | ASG Eye Hospital

The retina plays a vital role in vision, yet many retinal conditions develop silently and may not show symptoms until significant damage has occurred. Early diagnosis by a retina specialist can help protect vision and improve treatment outcomes.

Warning signs that need immediate attention:

• Sudden flashes of light
• New or increasing floaters
• Blurred or distorted vision
• A dark curtain or shadow in vision
• Difficulty reading or recognising faces
• Sudden vision loss

Common retina disorders include diabetic retinopathy, retinal detachment, macular degeneration, macular holes, and retinal tears. Many of these conditions respond better when diagnosed and treated early.

At ASG Eye Hospital, advanced retinal imaging and modern diagnostic technology help specialists detect retinal problems accurately and recommend the most appropriate retina treatment.

Available treatment options may include:

• Retinal laser treatment
• Intravitreal injections
• Vitrectomy surgery
• Retinal detachment repair
• Ongoing retinal monitoring

Delaying treatment can increase the risk of permanent vision loss. If you notice any sudden changes in your eyesight, seeking prompt evaluation from a qualified retina specialist is essential.

Book your retina consultation at ASG Eye Hospital today and take the first step toward protecting your vision.

Diabetes can affect your eyesight without obvious warning signs. Many people with diabetic eye disease experience no symptoms until retinal damage has already begun. Regular eye examinations are essential for protecting long-term vision.

Common symptoms to watch for include:

• Blurred or fluctuating vision
• Floaters or dark spots
• Difficulty reading
• Distorted vision
• Poor night vision
• Sudden vision changes

One of the most common diabetes-related eye conditions is diabetic retinopathy, which affects the blood vessels in the retina. Early detection through retinal screening can help prevent serious vision complications.

Protect your eye health by:

• Maintaining healthy blood sugar levels
• Monitoring blood pressure regularly
• Taking medications as prescribed
• Staying physically active
• Avoiding tobacco use
• Scheduling regular eye check-ups

For anyone young with high myopia facing cataract surgery and feeling scared — Dr. Maru is exactly who you want.

Seeing blur after LASIK? It's usually part of the healing process.

Mild blurry vision, light sensitivity, watery eyes, and fluctuating vision are common after LASIK. Most patients notice clearer vision within 24–48 hours as their eyes heal naturally.

Confused about whether to visit an Eye Specialist, Ophthalmologist, or Optometrist?

Many people use these terms interchangeably, but they play different roles in eye care. Knowing who to consult can help you get the right diagnosis and treatment without delay.

Here's a quick guide:
✅ Optometrist – Routine eye exams, vision testing, and prescription glasses or contact lenses.
✅ Ophthalmologist – Medical doctor who diagnoses eye diseases and performs surgeries like cataract, LASIK, glaucoma, and retina procedures.
✅ Eye Specialist – A general term commonly used for an ophthalmologist who provides comprehensive medical and surgical eye care.

At Asian Eye Institute & Laser Center, our experienced ophthalmologists provide advanced diagnosis and treatment for a wide range of eye conditions, helping you achieve the best possible vision.

Your Glasses Need a Break Too.

Experiencing blurry vision?

Blurry vision is one of the most common eye complaints, but it should never be ignored. It may be caused by simple refractive errors, digital eye strain, dry eyes, cataracts, diabetes, glaucoma, or retinal conditions.

Early diagnosis can help identify the cause and prevent potential vision complications.

Warning signs to watch for:
✔ Sudden blurry vision
✔ Difficulty reading or driving
✔ Frequent headaches
✔ Eye strain and fatigue
✔ Flashes or floaters
✔ Vision changes in one eye

Is your child squinting, rubbing their eyes frequently, or sitting too close to the TV?

These may be early signs of vision problems that should not be ignored. Many childhood eye conditions, including myopia (short-sightedness), lazy eye, and squint, can be managed more effectively when detected early.
